contract.task: Design a controlled real-model experiment comparing text prompts, pretokenized token-ID inputs, and cold/warm KV-prefix reuse for the existing Accord worktree.

Need bounded practical prototype in same worktree. No OpenAI API assumptions. Main question whether a prepared-token artifact and explicit cache reuse improve latency/cost without quality loss, beyond ordinary Python.

acceptance_criteria.description: Give a minimal factorial design isolating input representation from cache reuse, warmup/carryover effects, generation settings and complete chat template equality.
Define measurable speed, resource/cost and quality outcomes; distinguish local hardware cost from provider billing and cached-input accounting.
Propose a small repository-grounded task set with deterministic answers/checks and both exact-output equivalence and task accuracy; specify evidence and failure controls.
Save exact required result JSON to /private/tmp/accord-inference-design-result.json; do not perform model runs or edits.

result.summary: Proposed bounded real-model study: fixed llama.cpp server and Qwen3 8B, with a 2×2 design crossing complete rendered-text versus prepared token-ID input and empty versus reusable prefix KV state. Eight repository-derived diagnostic tasks and three counterbalanced repetitions give 96 measured generations, plus separately recorded setup/warmup/priming. Complete prompt-ID equality is a prerequisite; exact output equality and independent task accuracy are separate outcomes. This worker inspected source and the pinned server README but did not call the server or execute inference.

conclusions.claim: Use four cells: text/cold, IDs/cold, text/warm, IDs/warm. In the core comparison, render each complete chat prompt once outside request timing; the text cell tokenizes those exact rendered bytes on every request, while the IDs cell loads/validates a prepared artifact. Both then enter the same low-level inference function with equal IDs and generation settings. Measure optional per-request rendering as a separate operational scenario so a template-rendering saving is not mislabeled as a token-ID saving. Cold/warm varies only prefix KV reuse; model weights and kernel/runtime warmup stay equally warm. If the chosen backend cannot accept caller-supplied IDs or expose/reset prefix state, mark the affected cell unsupported and narrow the experiment rather than calling a text roundtrip a direct-ID trial. For the selected server, use the same /completion route with a string versus integer-array prompt, id_slot=0, and cache_prompt controlled explicitly. Native text timing must include server tokenization naturally; do not add a separate /tokenize network roundtrip to every text inference. Use /apply-template and /tokenize for preparation/equality checks outside core request timing, while accounting for their one-time artifact cost separately.

Freeze model identity/weights digest, quantization and dtype, backend/version, tokenizer/config digests, exact chat template and tool renderer, message roles/order, BOS/EOS/special-token policy, generation-prompt flag and any thinking mode. Persist messages, rendered bytes and hash, full IDs and hash, generation configuration, context limit and source hashes. Before any paired run, assert elementwise equality of the complete model-visible IDs, including all role/control tokens; do not infer equality from decoded text alone. Use fixed greedy decoding where supported, identical seed and all sampling/penalty/stop settings, batch size one, the same output cap, no truncation, and adequate output headroom. Record the effective settings rather than assuming backend defaults. The pinned README says string input may insert BOS according to model metadata while integer input does not trigger that rule. Match /tokenize add_special to that metadata, keep parse_special=true for rendered role tokens, and verify the actual full sequence. Request return_tokens=true to retain generated IDs; pin thinking behavior in the rendered prompt/settings.

Derive the reusable prefix from the longest common token prefix of the fully rendered task prompts, not by independently tokenizing and concatenating text fragments. Leave at least the final input token uncached if the backend needs it to produce the next-token distribution. Prime only this common source/instruction prefix; record exact prefix length, compatible model/config identity and priming time. Use an immutable prefix snapshot or clone/reset before every warm trial, never a previous task's generated suffix. Cold trials start with fresh empty KV state without reloading model weights. Assert matched cached tokens and remaining evaluated input tokens when observable; otherwise report requested reuse without claiming an observed cache hit. Hash IDs across the split and verify position/attention state. Do not pad prompts with changing nonces to force a miss: that changes the input treatment. The pinned server documents /slots/0?action=erase. For cold trials, erase and require zero observed cache reuse. For warm trials, erase, prime only the intended common prefix using a verified priming procedure, then issue the measured request with cache_prompt=true; retain priming overhead as a separate raw measurement. Avoid assuming that a zero-output priming request necessarily retains KV without checking it. Use prompt_progress.cache and, where returned, timings.cache_n/prompt_n; do not treat final tokens_cached alone as observed reused input. Keep global RAM prompt-cache settings in the manifest.

Before timing, run and discard a declared number of runtime warmups using disjoint prompts; then erase their slot KV state. Keep load/compile time separate. Proposed batch: eight tasks × four cells × three repetitions = 96 measured generations. For task i and repetition j, rotate the cell order by (i+j) modulo four; with eight tasks each cell occupies every position equally across the batch. Randomize task-block order using a recorded seed. Reinitialize/prime the intended slot state before every trial; global automatic cache behavior must be disabled or verified. Run one request at a time and no competing heavy jobs. Record order, process/device state and every raw timing; do not delete slow runs selectively. If runtime is tight, report the actual smaller sample as a pilot rather than claiming stable p95 or statistical equivalence. Use within-task paired differences, medians and ranges; repetitions measure noise, not additional independent tasks.

Use a fixed shared prefix containing the relevant production source and constants, with a short variable suffix asking for only JSON containing code and path. Keep test answers out of model context. The first four cases use max_chars=128000: (1) bounded_object({'evidence':[{'score':float('nan')}]}) → {'code':'invalid_json_value','path':'$.evidence[0].score'}; (2) bounded_object('{"evidence":[{"score":NaN}]}', allow_json=True) → {'code':'non_finite','path':'$.evidence[0].score'}; (3) bounded_object({'outer':{'a.b':[float('inf')]}}) → {'code':'invalid_json_value','path':'$.outer["a.b"][0]'}; (4) bounded_object({'a':'\ud800','b':[0]*101}) where a is an actual unpaired surrogate → {'code':'array_too_large','path':'$.b'}. The fourth specifically checks the previously regressed error precedence. Encode the surrogate as a literal escaped Python snippet in UTF-8 prompt text. Derive/freeze the golden JSON by invoking the source function in the parent's selected environment before model timing; compare against the cited tests. This worker has inspected the assertions, not executed those goldens. Extend the primary set to eight with (5) {"outer":[0]*100}, accepted → {"code":"accepted","path":"$"}; (6) {"outer":[0]*101} → array_too_large at $.outer; (7) {"outer":["x"*30]} with max_chars=20 → payload_too_large at $.outer[0]; (8) raw {"a":1,"a":2} with allow_json=True → duplicate_key at $. The accepted code is the experiment wrapper's explicit success convention, not a ContractError value. All eight share the same two-field JSON schema.

Report two quality axes independently: exact generated token-ID and decoded-byte equality across corresponding cells, and accuracy against the independent golden result after strict JSON parsing/schema validation. Record parse errors, unexpected fields, wrong code/path, truncation, stop reason, output-token count and raw outputs. Whitespace/key-order differences can preserve task accuracy while failing byte equality; identical wrong answers can pass equivalence while failing accuracy. Require all observed cases to retain accuracy for a pilot 'no observed task-quality loss' statement, with the denominator; do not generalize to coding ability. If greedy outputs differ, first investigate prompt IDs, prefix state, attention positions, numerical nondeterminism and stopping; preserve the discrepancy even if both outputs are correct. No answer repair, retries or prompt tuning after seeing arm outcomes unless recorded as a new experiment version. The pinned llama.cpp README explicitly warns that cache_prompt can change logits with different processing batch sizes; therefore output differences may be real numerical effects even with identical input tokens and greedy settings. Report them separately from accuracy changes rather than asserting deterministic equivalence.

Measure monotonic wall times for artifact preparation, per-request text encoding or ID read/validation/deserialization, cache prime/restore, prefill when the backend exposes it, first generated token and total completion. Report end-to-end TTFT starting before the selected input path and engine TTFT starting at inference entry. Explicitly synchronize asynchronous device work at measurement boundaries with backend-supported operations. Record input/prefix/evaluated/output token counts, decode tokens/s and transport artifact bytes including metadata. Keep prefill and decode distinct; equal-output paired runs support total-latency comparisons, while differing lengths require separate TTFT and output-length reporting. Record resident/peak memory and backend-reported device/KV allocation when available; a process-lifetime peak is not per-cell memory, and unavailable energy/GPU counters must be labeled unavailable. For this HTTP server, collect first content-token SSE time separately from progress/header arrival, and retain server prompt_ms/prompt_n/cache_n and predicted_ms/predicted_n where available. A local HTTP client cannot directly synchronize backend kernels; use server timings as the engine measure and client monotonic timestamps as end-to-end measurements, clearly labeled.

Local runs have no provider token invoice. Report elapsed time and measured resource use first; electricity or hardware amortization requires explicit measured energy and/or stated rate assumptions, shown as estimates. Prepared IDs do not by themselves reduce logical prompt-token count. Report cold-start artifact preparation and cache-priming costs separately from steady state, then for N requests include those costs once plus request costs; include cache storage/restore cost. A break-even estimate is setup_cost/(baseline_per_request minus optimized_per_request) only when the observed denominator is positive. Provider billing and cached-input accounting are a separate experiment requiring actual provider usage/cached-token fields and applicable prices; never treat an estimated saved prefill token or compressed byte as a billed-token saving.

Keep one JSONL record per trial plus a manifest with source/model/tokenizer/template/settings fingerprints and raw outputs. Run non-timed rejection controls for wrong tokenizer/template profile, changed source, altered IDs, stale/incompatible cache, and forced cache miss. A cache miss must reproduce the cold execution from complete tokens. Check that requested input/output fits the model context and all task data remains within explicit data delimiters. Mark OOM, unsupported features, timeouts and mismatch failures without replacing them with favorable retries. The existing packet verifier's requirement for exact decode-to-source roundtrip should not be assumed suitable for every chat tokenizer: the inference artifact's primary correctness invariant is equality to the IDs produced by the trusted full prompt renderer/tokenizer. Adopt observed conclusions only for the tested model/backend/configuration; ordinary Python can implement all these controls, and this experiment does not establish a need for language syntax.

evidence.description: Read current document: the prior probe uses embedding tokenizers only, excludes native chat framing and inference, and proposes separate portable messages, prepared tokens and engine-owned cache handles. Its next study explicitly calls for text/ID and cold/warm comparisons.

Read current evaluation report: the real task concerns nested diagnostic paths; initial structural validation and focused checks missed error-precedence regressions. Report distinguishes observed replay behavior from provider execution and favors a Python-accessible shared format.

Inspected _child_path, raw JSON parsing/localization and bounded_object. Source establishes escaped special-key paths, structural container limits, nonfinite distinctions and structural checks before UTF-8 encoding.

Inspected deterministic expected code/path assertions for nested nonfinite Python values, nonfinite raw JSON, special keys, size boundaries and structural-bound precedence over surrogate encoding failure. These tests were read, not run by this worker.

Inspected current profile fields, packet integrity checks, rejection controls and explicit no-inference/no-billing limitations. Existing render profile explicitly has no chat template; exact decode roundtrip is a probe invariant rather than a universal tokenizer property.
